items.title: Ripple-65B Preview: U.S. Open-Weight SOTA on Agentic Coding
items.summary: Ricursive Intelligence released Ripple-65B Preview, a 65-billion-parameter open-weight model that achieves U.S. open-weight state-of-the-art on agentic coding benchmarks with a TerminalBench 2.1 score of 80.52. The model was trained for $32M, which is one-tenth the cost of the previous open-weight SOTA, and utilizes a dense architecture optimized for efficient training and serving on NVIDIA hardware.
items.why_it_matters: The model offers a cost-effective alternative for agentic coding tasks, achieving top-tier performance at a fraction of the training cost of previous state-of-the-art models while running efficiently on local devices like the NVIDIA DGX Spark.
items.next_step_detail: Download the model checkpoint and benchmark it against your existing coding‑agent model (e.g., GPT‑4o).
items.verification_note: Ripple-65B Preview is a 65-billion-parameter open-weight model

items.title: garrytan / gstack
items.summary: gstack is an open-source tool that configures coding agents like Claude Code to function as a virtual engineering team with specific roles such as CEO, eng manager, and QA lead. It operates via slash commands and Markdown files under an MIT license.
items.why_it_matters: It provides structured roles and automated workflows for review, QA, and release processes, which the source states are used to run multiple sprints simultaneously.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and run `npm install && npm start` to explore the built‑in agents.

items.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro model weights are out
items.summary: Kimi K3.1 Pro is an open-weight, natively multimodal agentic model with 2.8T total parameters and 104B activated parameters, featuring a 1-million-token context window. It is post-trained from Kimi K3 using large-scale joint reinforcement learning across hundreds of downstream domains.
items.why_it_matters: The model offers substantial improvements in coding, 3D creation, financial research, and factual accuracy, along with a 1-million-token context window for agentic capabilities.
items.next_step_detail: git clone https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro and run a quick generation test with transformers.

items.title: Progress on provable inference for large language models
items.summary: Anthropic researchers present FlashProve, a system using zkSNARKs to cryptographically prove that a model's output originates from a specific LLM, achieving proof generation speeds of approximately 110 tokens per second on a single H100 GPU. The system hides model weights while allowing users to verify responses without access to the model's internal parameters.
items.why_it_matters: It enables users to verify that responses come from the specific model they requested, addressing scenarios where independent evaluators need assurance of model identity or clients using third-party routing services need to confirm they are receiving tokens from the model they paid for.
items.next_step_detail: Read the Anthropic blog post and note any verification primitives you can adopt in your deployment.

items.title: Your Documentation Is Out of Date. Let an AI Agent Keep It in Sync
items.summary: An AI agent skill named sync-docs uses Git commit metadata in Markdown frontmatter to identify documentation drift and automatically updates files to match the current source code implementation. The agent inspects changes since the last recorded commit to verify accuracy before opening a pull request with the corrected documentation.
items.why_it_matters: It addresses the common problem of documentation drifting away from source code by delegating the continuous maintenance task to an agent that ensures technical docs accurately reflect the current system state.
items.next_step_detail: Follow the repo link in the article, install the agent, and point it at a sample repo to see auto‑doc updates.

items.title: FareedKhan-dev / kimi-k3-in-c
items.summary: A 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 model runs inference on a single CPU using 8.24 GB of RAM, implemented in portable C99 without BLAS, frameworks, or a GPU. The project includes benchmarks, examples, and tests for this zero-dependency inference engine.
items.why_it_matters: It provides a zero-dependency, memory-efficient implementation for running large language models on consumer hardware.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and run `make run` to benchmark inference on your workstation.

items.title: ArXiv: SUMONE: A Simple and Efficient Summarizer for Plug-and-Play Agent Memory
items.summary: SUMONE is a standalone summarizer trained via masked reconstruction to compact agent interaction histories without task-specific supervision. It reduces estimated inference costs by approximately 78% on DeepSearchQA and 75% on SWE-bench Verified relative to full context.
items.why_it_matters: The method enables plug-and-play context compression for unchanged agents, transferring across downstream models and harnesses without additional fine-tuning.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and run the provided benchmark script on your agent codebase.

items.title: HF Paper: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning Improves Long Horizon Agents
items.summary: This paper trains a draft model to reject critical reasoning tokens, forcing the target model to verify them directly to reduce numerical noise in long-horizon agents. This approach raises end-to-end success rates on agentic coding benchmarks by training only 0.06% to 0.28% of hosted parameters without altering the target model's output distribution.
items.why_it_matters: It recasts speculative decoding from a pure accelerator into an active allocator for context precision that improves the accuracy of long-horizon agents.
items.next_step_detail: Review the methodology section and consider a proof‑of‑concept integration with your agent executor.

items.title: I Built a Judge My AI Couldn't Influence. In 51 Runs, It Never Gave a B.
items.summary: RUMI is an autonomous scientific discovery engine that searches live literature, builds knowledge graphs, and generates hypotheses through a multi-stage adversarial refinement process. External evaluation of 51 runs revealed that its self-assessment is uncalibrated and uncorrelated with external scores, with the system failing to produce resolvable citations despite retrieving real papers.
items.why_it_matters: The engine's self-assessment functions as an unreliable narrative rather than a measurement, making it unsuitable as a training signal or stopping criterion for autonomous agents.
items.next_step_detail: Read the post to understand the evaluation architecture and consider reusing the judge pattern.
